Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
8:30 PM

People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying quicker and easier than cash, cards or net banking, and it now works almost everywhere.

Anyone with a bank account and a phone can pay in seconds by scanning a QR code or typing a mobile number. The money goes straight from one bank account to another, with a PIN needed for each payment. Tea stalls, vegetable sellers and big shops all accept it, so many people rarely carry cash.

Three main reasons:

Free and instant: Most payments between people and at shops cost the payer nothing, and the money arrives in seconds, at any hour, on any day.
One simple setup: One app works with any bank. A single UPI ID or QR code replaces card machines, account numbers and IFSC codes.
Easy for small sellers: A printed QR code is enough to accept payments, with no machine and no monthly rental. That is why even street vendors have joined.

Early cashback offers, government support, cheap smartphones and affordable mobile data helped it become a daily habit for hundreds of millions of people. The app also keeps a clear record of every payment, which cash never does.
